extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers interested in social and political criticism (early 20th‑century)
extracted.subtask_description: An argumentative essay critiquing modern social reformers and defenders of institutions (family, property, state), offering interpretive standards for judging reforms and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mending versus Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: You mend a thing because you like it; you end a thing because you don't. To mend is to strengthen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this distinction to decide whether an institution should be reformed or abolished. Chesterton contrasts Socialists (who 'mend' the state) with anarchists (who would end both state and family), and argues one should only 'mend' institutions one values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Public from Private (umbrella vs stick)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential error of some reformers is to treat private, personal things like public, shared things — 'a Socialist means a man who thinks a walking-stick like an umbrella because they both go into the umbrella-stand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize which goods/activities belong to the state (public protection, standard services) and which belong to individual personality and taste (personal belongings, ceremonial objects); avoid applying public solutions to personal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate Communal Solutions: uniform tasks vs personal arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain activities (e.g., washing) are essentially uniform and public-friendly; others (e.g., cooking) are arts of personality and should remain individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communal laundries might suit the one-right-way tasks, but communal kitchens misunderstand the nature of cooking as personal and perverse art — policy must discriminate accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware Strengthening Government at Cost of Personal Liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: Many social reforms 'sharpen' governmental machinery, making government stronger (and sometimes harsher) while leaving the private realm weakened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reforms by whether they increase coercive power unnecessarily inside the private outline of life; progress that increases police/state control at the expense of liberty is suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: To Preserve Family Life, Address Economic Causes (redistribute property)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poor are too impoverished to be domestic; to preserve family life one must equalize property and redistribute wealth, not merely preach family virtues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy aimed at saving the family should include substantial economic measures (e.g., buy-outs of landlordism, peasant proprietorship) rather than only moral exhortation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attack Root Causes, Not Symptoms (lice vs slums)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is wrong to punish or alter the victims (cut poor girls' hair to stop lice) instead of removing the underlying cause (slums, poverty, usurious landlords).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social policy must target structural causes (housing, poverty, landlordism) rather than imposing coercive, cosmetic fixes on the poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of Political and Artistic Sanity: fit institutions to 'flesh and spirit'
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions should be judged by whether they fit the normal flesh and spirit (preserve customary, human practices like keeping one's head and hair).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies or reforms that erase or mutilate ordinary human customs or arts undermine the conservatism necessary for popular resistance and cultural continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect Positive Popular Prejudices in Democratic Change
rubrics_metrics.description: Democracy aims at the will of the people, not merely their votes; it is undemocratic to give people rights against their will when they hold a positive prejudice (e.g., some women view the vote as 'unwomanly').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish passive indifference from active opposition; reforms that ignore sincere popular attachments risk making democracy a farce and should focus on persuasion rather than imposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep Cleanliness in Proper Hierarchy (soap vs soul)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chesterton criticizes the 'idolatry of mere ablution' — cleanliness is important but must not be worshipped above moral and spiritual goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insist on teaching cleanliness but avoid making it the highest value; regard material luxuries (soap) as things to be furnished by improving living standards rather than as sole ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer Decentralized Property (peasant proprietorship) to State Concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: The solution to concentrated property is to 'unconcentrate' it; distributed ownership (peasant proprietorship) is morally and socially preferable to concentration in trusts or the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate policies like buying out landlordism gradually (example: Wyndham's Act in Ireland) to decentralize ownership rather than immediate confiscation or centralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose Collusion Between Supposed Opposites (Hudge and Gudge partnership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reformers and plutocrats may, in practice, play into each other's hands: idealistic rhetoric can produce consequences that benefit plutocracy and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically examine whether opposing political rhetoric actually perpetuates the same harms (e.g., keeping the common man homeless) and evaluate actors by effects, not labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore and Define Natural Domestic Functions to Mend the Family
rubrics_metrics.description: If one truly wants to preserve family, one must accept the natural distinctions and restraints of roles (father, mother, child) and work to strengthen those functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and reform aimed at family renewal should include deliberate measures to support the practical conditions (economic, legal, cultural) in which traditional domestic roles can function.
